messages:
maya: Heads up — NVIDIA published a couple of advisories that look relevant to our stack: CVE-2026-XXXX (CUDA runtime async API / cuasync) and CVE-2026-YYYY (cuDNN conv kernel memory bounds). Not public exploit yet, but severity looks medium-high. Can we quickly map impact across driver versions 535.* and CUDA 12.2 + cuDNN 9 + NCCL 2.17?

josh: Thanks. Do we have the exact CVSS scores and whether the issue is kernel-driver vs userland?

deploy-bot: Automated vuln scan summary:
- CVE-2026-XXXX: CVSS 7.3 (privileged local/remote race in CUDA runtime async). Affects libcuda.so and cuda runtime packages.
- CVE-2026-YYYY: CVSS 6.8 (out-of-bounds in cuDNN convolution kernels). Affects cuDNN <=9.0.1.
Detected in images: rdi/gpu-runtime:2026-03-01, rdi/dedicated-runtime:2026-02-20

devon: From initial read, cuasync is userland but touches driver APIs; cuDNN OOB is purely userland kernels. Driver kernel module appears not directly vulnerable, but we need to validate our patched driver path.

ana: @maya @josh tagging SRE — if we need to patch drivers on Dedicated clusters we should plan a staged rollout. Add audit events for any driver/package install.

maya: Agreed. Immediate plan suggestion (short):
1) Confirm whether our driver bundles (535.54/535.67) expose the libcuda symbols referenced.
2) Run the cuDNN conv regression test suite on canaries (cpu/gpu mix).
3) If userland only -> prioritize cuDNN/CUDA package update in images (P2), but if driver ABI impacted -> P1 and coordinate kernel module rollout with SRE.
4) Add RBAC + audit log entry for any manual driver push to private clusters.

josh: I'll run quick checks on prod-canary nodes. Commands to collect versions:```
# on host
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version || modinfo nvidia | head -n 5
# in container images
dpkg -l | egrep "cuda|cudnn|nvidia" || rpm -qa | egrep "cuda|cudnn|nvidia"
```

josh: Update: prod-canary nodes show driver 535.54, CUDA 12.2, cuDNN 9.0.0. Our runtime image rdi/gpu-runtime:2026-03-01 includes cuDNN 9.0.0 (vulnerable per bot).

devon: I'll trigger the cuDNN conv regression harness against that runtime image and post failures. If we see deterministic OOBs we'll need to pin to patched cuDNN 9.0.2 and run quick latency/regression checks.

maya: KMS note: for Private deployments we should ensure any driver/package artifacts are KMS-signed and verified at install. We had that on the backlog — moving it up to high. Also audit logs for package install should include who triggered, image digest, and KMS key id.

ana: Also consider fallback policy: if a region sees driver instability, smart routing -> fallback to host with different driver (or CPU path) for low-priority workloads. Add this to the incident runbook.

josh: Running smoke tests now. ETA ~45m.

deploy-bot: CVE ticket created: SEC-2026-1758 (linked CVEs CVE-2026-XXXX,CVE-2026-YYYY). Assigned -> maya, devon. Patch window requested: 48h for canary, 7d for fleet (if P1).

maya: Action items: @devon run conv-regression + nightly perf check; @josh enumerate affected customer Dedicated pools and open customer comms draft; @ana prep canary rollout playbook with rollback steps and audit hooks; I'll start KMS-signing spec doc.

devon: Quick note — NCCL doesn't look directly affected but we'll run the NCCL collective perf tests to be safe. Also will validate quantized kernels in our runtimes.

ana: If we need an emergency driver kernel rebuild, flag to infra early — that could require reboots and will impact Dedicated SLA.

josh: Canary results: cuDNN conv harness shows intermittent OOB when running fused-conv + workspace=auto on some inputs, reproducible on one node (log excerpt attached). No kernel oops observed.

maya: Based on that, move cuDNN to P1 for image update and validation. Driver patch P2 for now but keep monitoring for any kernel-level reports.

devon: I'll build image with cuDNN 9.0.2 + CUDA 12.2 and run the full perf/regression matrix across canaries overnight. Posting build id when ready.

maya: Good. Keep thread updated. If anything escalates to kernel / exploit, raise to P0 and loop in exec + customer success. :white_check_mark:

(End of thread)
